title: Who is the Customer? Adventure
welcome_lead: No customers, no business. Today we meet the people who pay. 🎯
meta_desc: Marketing & Customers Adventure 1 — KS3 Business Studies on target markets, customer needs and segmentation.
final_note: You learned who customers are, how businesses group them, and why their needs matter most.

concepts.def: A person who buys a product or service
The person who actually uses it
A smaller part of a wider market

walkthroughs.body_html:
A customer is the buyer. The consumer is the user.

Example: a mum buys cereal (customer), her child eats it (consumer). The advert must please both! 🥣

Businesses pick a target market — the group most likely to buy.

Lego targets children 4–12. Rolex targets wealthy adults.

If you try to please everyone, you please no one.

A segment is a slice of the market grouped by something they share:

  • Age — teens, OAPs.
  • Income — luxury vs budget.
  • Lifestyle — vegan, sporty, gamer.
  • Location — town vs country.

Smart marketing matches the message to the segment. 🎯

mcqs.q: Why are hygiene factors and motivators not on the same scale in Herzberg's theory?
options: Hygiene factors only prevent dissatisfaction (their absence demotivates, presence is neutral); motivators create satisfaction (their presence motivates, absence is neutral). They affect different outcomes, not different points on one scale.
Hygiene factors are about workplace cleanliness only.
CSR is the legal requirement to pay taxes.
Hygiene factors and motivators are just two types of motivation that combine.

mcqs.q: Why might a business adopt corporate social responsibility (CSR)?
options: Hygiene factors are about workplace cleanliness only.
CSR is purely about being ethical with no business benefit.
Reasons include genuine ethics, but also commercial benefits — improved reputation, customer loyalty, employee retention, and reduced regulatory or reputational risk.
CSR is the legal requirement to pay taxes.

mcqs.q: What is a key disadvantage of being a sole trader?
options: Hygiene factors are about workplace cleanliness only.
Unlimited liability — the owner's personal assets are at risk if the business fails, because there is no legal separation between owner and business.
Sole traders must employ at least one other person by law.
The main disadvantage is that sole traders can't sell any products.
